1422.01 DESIGNATION OF DIVISION OF BUILDING AND ZONING INSPECTION; COMPOSITION.
   (a)   Designation. The Division of Building and Zoning Inspection within the
Department of Public Service shall be known and designated as the Division of
Building and Zoning Inspection in this Code.
   (b)   Composition. The Division of Building and Zoning Inspection shall
consist of the Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection, the Assistant
Superintendent and a Plans Examiner.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1422.02 DESIGNATION OF SUPERINTENDENT OF BUILDING AND ZONING INSPECTION.
   The Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection shall be known and
designated as the Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection in matters
pertaining to the enforcement of this Building and Housing Code, other
ordinances of the City and regulations and laws of the State assigned to him or
her for enforcement.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1422.03 QUALIFICATIONS OF SUPERINTENDENT OF BUILDING AND ZONING INSPECTION;
ASSISTANT SUPERINTENDENT.
   To be eligible for appointment, the Superintendent of Building and Zoning
Inspection shall be a registered architect, registered engineer, Building
Inspector or Superintendent of Construction, within the last ten years, with at
least five years of experience in building construction. He or she shall be
generally informed on the quality and strength of building construction, on
good practice in fire prevention, on the accepted requirements for safe exit
facilities and on the proper installation of plumbing and sanitary conditions
of occupants of buildings. He or she shall be in good health and physically
capable of making the necessary examinations and inspections of buildings in
the course of construction. He or she shall not have any interest whatever,
directly or indirectly, in the sale or manufacture of any material, process or
device entering into or used in or in connection with building construction.
   The Administrative Officer may appoint an Assistant to the Superintendent of
Building and Zoning Inspection, subject, however, to confirmation by a majority
vote of the members of Council. The Assistant to the Superintendent of Building
and Zoning Inspection shall be a part-time employee, shall work under the
direction, supervision and control of the Superintendent, shall be in the
unclassified service and shall work a maximum of ten hours per week at such
compensation as Council shall from time to time establish.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1422.04 MANAGEMENT AND ENFORCEMENT RESPONSIBILITY OF SUPERINTENDENT OF BUILDING
AND ZONING INSPECTION.
   The Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection shall be the active
head of the Division of Building and Zoning Inspection and he or she shall have
the management of all matters and affairs pertaining thereto. For the
application and enforcement of this Building and Housing Code, other ordinances
of the City and regulations and laws of the State, assigned to the
Superintendent for enforcement, he or she may assign any duties and authority
provided to him or her under such ordinances, regulations or law, to any duly
appointed employee of the Division of Building and Zoning Inspection. The
Superintendent may alter assignments of duties and authority as he or she deems
best for the efficiency and proper operation of the Division.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1422.05 CONFLICTS OF INTEREST.
   No officer or employee connected with the Division of Building and Zoning
Inspection, except one whose only connection is as a member of a board
established by this Code, shall be financially interested in the furnishing of
labor, material or appliances for the construction, alteration or maintenance
of a building, or in the making of plans or specifications thereof, unless he
or she is the owner of such building. No such officer or employee shall engage
in any work which is inconsistent with his or her duties or with the interests
of the Division of Building and Zoning Inspection.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1422.06 DUTIES OF SUPERINTENDENT OF BUILDING AND ZONING INSPECTION.
   Except as otherwise required, the Superintendent of Building and Zoning
Inspection or his or her duly authorized representative shall receive
applications, issue permits and licenses and furnish the prescribed
certificates as required by this Building and Housing Code, except as provided
by the City Charter. He or she shall examine premises for which permits have
been issued and shall make necessary inspections to see that the provisions of
this Building and Housing Code and other pertinent laws and ordinances are
complied with and that construction is prosecuted safely. He or she shall
enforce all laws, ordinances and regulations relating to the construction,
alteration, repair, removal, moving, demolition, equipment, use and occupancy,
location and maintenance of buildings and structures, except as may be
otherwise provided for. He or she shall, when requested by the Director of
Public Service or Council, or when the interests of the City so require, make
investigations in connection with matters referred to in this Building and
Housing Code and render reports on the same. For the purpose of enforcing
compliance with the provision of this Building and Housing Code and other
pertinent laws and ordinances assigned to him or her for enforcement, he or she
shall issue such notices or orders as may be necessary.
   Nothing contained in this Building and Housing Code shall exempt the
Director of Public Service, the Chief of Police, the Fire Chief, the Director
of the Department of Health, or any other officer or employee of the City, from
his or her obligation of enforcing those provisions of this Building and
Housing Code or any other law or ordinance which comes within his or her sphere
of authority.
   The Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection shall also be the
Zoning Administrator for the City and is hereby directed and authorized to see
that the Zoning Code is complied with.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1422.07 MAINTENANCE OF RECORDS.
   The Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection shall keep careful and
comprehensive records of applications, permits and/or certificates issued,
inspections made and reports rendered. He or she shall retain on file, if
possible, all drawings submitted to him or her to obtain building permits, so
long as any part of the building or structure for which the plan was submitted
may be in existence, except that plans for private dwellings and minor
buildings need not be kept on file more than three months after the final
approval of the building.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1422.08 REPORTS TO DIRECTOR OF PUBLIC SERVICE AND DIRECTOR OF FINANCE.
   The Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection shall make a report to
the Director of Public Service and to the Director of Finance once each month,
or more often if requested. The monthly report shall include statements of
permits and/or certificates issued and other relevant matters as desired.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1422.09 COOPERATION FROM OTHER OFFICIALS.
   The Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection may request and shall
receive, so far as may be necessary in the discharge of his or duties, the
assistance and cooperation of the Director of Public Service in fixing grades,
the Chief of Police in enforcing orders, the Fire Chief in the handling of
interrelated work, and of other City officials.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1422.10 BADGE OF OFFICE; CREDENTIALS.
   For the purpose of identification, the Superintendent of Building and Zoning
Inspection shall adopt a badge of office which he or she or his or her
authorized representative shall display on demand, provided that in an
emergency any other method of identification shall be sufficient.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1422.11 IMPERSONATING A DIVISION OF BUILDING AND ZONING INSPECTION EMPLOYEE.
   No person, not a duly appointed employee of the Division of Building and
Zoning Inspection, shall falsely represent himself or herself as being an
employee of the Division.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1422.12 RIGHT OF ENTRY.
   (a)   The Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection and the duly
appointed employees of the Division of Building and Zoning Inspection shall, at
any reasonable time in the performance of their duties and under the conditions
set forth in this Building and Housing Code, have the right to enter upon any
premises, building or structure in instances and under conditions not in
violation of the Constitution or laws of the State or the United States.
   (b)   When his or her duties require the Superintendent to enter any
building, structure or premises to handle a hazardous situation requiring
immediate action, he or she may authorize such persons as he or she deems
necessary to handle the situation, to enter such building, structure or
premises.
   (c)   No person shall obstruct or abuse an employee of the Division of
Building and Zoning Inspection in the performance of his or her duties.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1422.13 INSPECTIONS.
   (a)   With the exception of inspections required to be made by the Director
of Public Service, the Chief of Police, the Fire Chief, the Director of Public
Health, or other officers or employees of the City, inspections required for
the enforcement of the provisions of this Building and Housing Code shall be
made by the Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection or his or her duly
authorized representative, except that the Superintendent may accept reports of
inspectors of recognized inspection services, if, after investigation, he or
she is satisfied as to the qualifications and reliability of the inspection
service under consideration. No certificate called for by any provision of this
Building and Housing Code shall be based on reports of inspection services
unless such reports are in writing and are certified by a responsible officer
of such inspection service. The Superintendent may require supervision of work
and certificates of inspection as provided in Section
1426.16.
   (b)   All new buildings, structures and additions under construction, and
all alterations or repairs to buildings when regulated by this Building and
Housing Code, shall be inspected as follows:
      (1)   An inspection shall be made before pouring footers, as per the
rules and regulations made by the Superintendent.
      (2)   An inspection shall be made after the foundation has been erected
and before any backfilling or the erection of any portion of the building.
      (3)   A rough inspection shall be made after all mechanicals are
installed. The mechanical inspection must be stamped on the building permit
card or recorded in the inspection office. No concrete floors shall be poured
before this rough inspection.
      (4)   Final inspection shall include all items ready for occupancy.
   (c)   All new buildings or structures, and all additions, alterations and
repairs to existing buildings or structure, which, when completed, will have
all of the framing and structural parts exposed sufficiently to make a proper
inspection practicable, shall be inspected when work is completed.
   (d)   All installations and all additions, alterations and repairs to
existing installations, for which permits are required, shall be inspected
before being used.
   (e)   For the purpose of insuring that proper inspections will be made of
new buildings and structures under construction, of additions and alterations
or repairs to existing buildings and structures, of buildings to be moved or
razed, or of installations and additions, alterations or repairs thereto, the
contractor performing the work on any job for which a permit has been issued,
or the owner to whom a permit has been issued when no contractor is employed,
shall notify the Superintendent of the time, as provided herein, to make such
inspection. The notification for inspection shall be given at a time which will
give the Superintendent a reasonable amount of time to make or cause the
inspection to be made, and this time shall be as follows:
      (1)   For inspections as required in subsections (a) and (b) hereof, the
Superintendent shall be notified not less than forty-eight hours before the
next stage of work is to begin or the building or structure is to be occupied.
      (2)   For inspections as required in subsection (c) hereof, or where
occupancy is not a consideration, such as signs, billboards, retaining walls,
etc., the Superintendent shall be notified when any preliminary inspections are
required or necessary, and, for final inspection, not later than forty-eight
hours after the structure has been completed.
      (3)   For inspections as required in subsection (d) hereof, the
Superintendent shall be notified not less than forty-eight hours before any
part of an installation which requires inspection is covered in a manner which
would make a proper inspection unnecessarily difficult and, in every case,
before such installation is used.
   (f)   In addition to the inspections required to be made at the request of
an owner or a contractor, the Superintendent shall, as he or she deems
necessary during the progress of the work, inspect all operations for which
permits have been issued. The Superintendent shall make a record of every such
inspection and of all violations found as a result thereof.
   (g)   When deemed necessary by him or her, the Superintendent shall make an
inspection of materials or assemblies at the point of manufacture or
fabrication. He or she shall make a record of every such examination and
inspection and of all items and details found wherein such materials or
assemblies do not meet the requirements of this Building and Housing Code.
   (h)   Existing buildings, structures and installations shall be inspected by
the Superintendent as often as is deemed necessary by him or her.
   (i)   An inspection required to be made by the Director of Public Service,
the Director of Public Health, the Chief of Police or the Fire Chief shall be
made at the time required by law or ordinance and when directed by the director
of the department or chief of the division obligated to make such inspection.
   (j)   The Superintendent shall be given not less than forty-eight hours
after the filing of an application for a permit to move or raze a building, to
inspect such building to determine if it can be safely moved or razed in the
manner proposed and whether or not the proposed location thereof, if the
building is to be moved, is in compliance with the ordinances of the City
applicable thereon.
   For the purpose of this section only, each day that the Municipal Building
is open for regular business shall be applicable as time of notification
(Saturdays, Sundays and holidays are not counted in the time period).
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1422.14 VIOLATION REPORTS AND NOTICE.
   All reports that a condition exists or that an operation is being performed
in violation of this Building and Housing Code, or of any law or ordinance
assigned to the Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection for
enforcement, may be required to be made in writing, and shall bear the
signature of the person making such report when written.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1422.15 PROSECUTION FOR VIOLATIONS.
   (a)   The Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection may cause the
prosecution of any person who violates any provision of this Building and
Housing Code, or who fails to comply therewith or with any of the requirements
thereof, or who erects, constructs, alters, repairs or equips, or has erected,
constructed, altered, repaired or equipped, a building or structure, in
violation of a detailed statement or plan submitted and approved thereunder, or
of a permit or certificate issued thereunder.
   (b)   The Superintendent may cause the prosecution of the owner of a
building, structure or premises where anything in violation of this Building
and Housing Code is placed or exists, and an architect, builder, contractor,
agent, person or corporation employed in connection therewith and who may have
assisted in the commission of such violation.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1422.16 NOTICE OF VIOLATIONS.
   Whenever the Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection is satisfied
that a building or structure, or any work in connection therewith, the
erection, construction, alteration, execution or repair of which is regulated,
permitted or prohibited by this Building and Housing Code, is being erected,
constructed, altered or repaired in violation of the provisions or requirements
of this Building and Housing Code, or in violation of a detailed statement or
plan submitted and approved thereunder, or of a permit or certificate issued
thereunder, he or she may serve a written notice or order upon the person
responsible therefor, directing the discontinuance of such illegal action and
the remedying of the condition that is in violation of the provisions or
requirements of this Building and Housing Code.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1422.17 FAILURE TO COMPLY WITH ORDER; ENFORCEMENT.
   In case the notice or order referred to in Section
1422.16 is not promptly complied with, the Superintendent of Building and
Zoning Inspection may request the Solicitor to institute an appropriate action
or proceeding at law or in equity to restrain, correct or remove such
violation, or the execution of work thereon, or to restrain or correct the
erection or alteration of, or require the removal of, or to prevent the
occupation or use of, the building or structure erected, constructed or altered
in violation of or not in compliance with the provisions of this Building and
Housing Code or with respect to which the requirements thereof, or of any order
or direction made pursuant to provisions contained herein, shall not have been
complied with.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1422.18 REMOVAL OF NOTICES PROHIBITED.
   No person, not authorized to do so by the Superintendent of Building and
Zoning Inspection, shall remove or cause to be removed any notice or other
matter posted or caused to be posted by the Superintendent in the application
of any provision of this Building and Housing Code.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1422.19 STOP WORK ORDERS.
   Whenever, in the opinion of the Superintendent of Building and Zoning
Inspection, by reason of defective, reckless, careless or other illegal work in
violation of a provision or requirement of this Building and Housing Code, the
continuance of a building operation is contrary to public welfare and safety,
or when a required permit has not been obtained or has not been posted as
required in Section
1426.22, he or she may order, either orally or in writing, all further work to
be stopped and may require suspension of work until the condition in violation
has been remedied.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1422.20 PERMIT REVOCATION AND POSTING; FURTHER WORK PROHIBITED.
   The Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection may revoke a permit or
approval, issued under the provisions of this Building and Housing Code, in
case there has been any false statements or misrepresentation as to a material
fact in the application or plans on which the permit or approval was based.
Written notice of such revocation, signed by the Superintendent, shall be
mailed to the address of the owner as given in the application for the permit
or in a case when the owner is out of the City, or, after reasonable search,
cannot be located, such notice shall be handed to or mailed to his or her agent
or contractor, and revocation shall be posted on the premises where the permit
is required to be posted. No person shall perform any work in or about a
building or structure after the revocation of the permit therefore and the
posting of the notice thereof, except to perform such work as may be required
for the correcting of the existing violations and for the protection of
completed work pending an appeal of such revocation.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1422.99 GENERAL CODE PENALTY; EQUITABLE REMEDIES.
   (a)   Whoever violates any provision of this Building and Housing Code, or
fails to comply therewith, or with any of the requirements thereof, or erects,
constructs, alters or repairs, or has erected, constructed, altered or
repaired, a building or structure, in violation of a detailed statement or plan
submitted and approved thereunder, or of a permit or certificate issued
thereunder, is guilty of a minor misdemeanor for a first offense; for a second
offense within one year after the first offense, such person is guilty of a
misdemeanor of the fourth degree. Each day during or on which a violation or
noncompliance occurs or continues, after the offender has been notified of such
violation or of such failure to comply, shall constitute a separate offense.
   (b)   The owner of a building, structure or premises, where anything in
violation of this Building and Housing Code is placed or exists, and an
architect, engineer, builder, contractor, agent, person or corporation employed
in connection therewith and who may have assisted in the commission of such
violation, are each guilty of a minor misdemeanor for a first offense; for a
second offense within one year after the first offense, such person is guilty
of a misdemeanor of the fourth degree. Each day during or on which a violation
or noncompliance occurs or continues, after the offender has been notified of
such violation or of such failure to comply, shall constitute a separate
offense.
   (c)   Whoever knowingly and willfully obstructs or abuses a duly appointed
employee of the Division of Building and Zoning Inspection in the performance
of his or her duties is guilty of a minor misdemeanor for a first offense; for
a second offense within one year after the first offense, such person is guilty
of a misdemeanor of the fourth degree. Each incident of obstruction or abuse
shall constitute a separate offense.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
   (d)   The application of the penalties provided in this section shall not be
deemed to prevent the enforced removal of prohibited conditions or the
application of any other equitable remedy.
CHAPTER 1424
Board of Zoning and Building Appeals
1424.01   Jurisdiction.
1424.02   Rules and procedures.
1424.03   Powers and duties.
1424.04   Appeals from Superintendent’s decision; procedure; fees.
1424.05   Public hearing required.
   CROSS REFERENCES
   Appeals under Zoning Code - see P. & Z.
1254.05 et seq.
   Division of Building and Zoning Inspection - see B. & H.
1422.01
   Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection - see B. & H.
1422.02 et seq.
   Appeals under International Property Maintenance Code - see B. & H.
1496.08
1424.01 JURISDICTION.
   The Board of Zoning and Building Appeals shall have the power to hear and
decide appeals for exceptions to, and variances in, the application of
resolutions, ordinances, regulations, measures and orders of administrative
officials or agencies governing zoning and building in the City, as may be
required to afford justice and avoid unreasonable hardship, subject to such
reasonable standards as shall be prescribed by Council, and such other powers
as may be granted to it by Council.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1424.02 RULES AND PROCEDURES.
   (a)   The Board of Zoning and Building Appeals may adopt its own rules of
procedure, not inconsistent with this Building and Housing Code, and may change
the same at its discretion. The final disposition of an appeal or the adoption
of any rule or regulation or amendment thereto shall be in the form of a
resolution. When a decision of the Superintendent of Building and Zoning
Inspection is appealed, such resolution shall either reverse, modify or affirm
the decision or determination appealed from. An affirmative vote of a majority
of the members appointed to the Board shall be necessary to adopt any rule or
resolution or an amendment to a rule or resolution. The Board shall render a
decision on an appeal within twenty-one days after notice thereof has been
filed as required in Section
1424.04(b), and on the adoption of a rule or regulation, or an amendment
thereto, within ninety days after the application therefor has been filed as
provided in this Building and Housing Code.
   (b)   A copy of the minutes of the proceedings and a copy of any resolutions
resulting from such a hearing shall be signed by the Chairperson, or by the
Vice-Chairperson in the absence of the Chairperson, and by the Secretary of the
Board, shall bear all approvals required by this Building and Housing Code and
shall be sent by mail or otherwise to the appellant or applicant, as the case
may be. A signed copy of the minutes and resolutions shall be filed with the
Clerk of Council and with the Division of Building and Zoning Inspection and
shall be open to public inspection.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1424.03 POWERS AND DUTIES.
   For the purpose of carrying out the intent and purpose of this Building and
Housing Code, the Board of Zoning and Building Appeals shall have the following
powers and perform the following duties:
   (a)   To hear any appeal, filed as provided for in this Building and Housing
Code, by any person adversely affected by a decision of the Superintendent of
Building and Zoning Inspection in the enforcement of this Building and Housing
Code, and to determine whether, in the opinion of the Board, a decision of the
Superintendent should be reversed, modified or affirmed. The Board shall have
the power and authority to require, by resolution, that the Superintendent
modify, reverse, or enforce his or her decision.
   (b)   To formulate and report to Council, from time to time, recommendations
for action by Council upon such amendments in existing ordinances, relating to
the purposes declared in Section
1420.03, as public health and safety and the development of the arts and
sciences may from time to time require.
   (c)   To formulate and report to Council, from time to time, recommendations
for action by Council upon such additional legislation as it may recommend with
a view to carrying out fully, by ordinance, the purposes declared in Section
1420.03.
   (d)   To determine by rule or regulation, or an amendment thereto, on any
application made, that any particular fixture, device, material, system or
method or manner of construction may be used, whenever the use of such fixture,
device, material, system or method or manner of construction is determined to
be equivalent to that described in any section of this Building and Housing
Code, as regards the standards and purposes of this Building and Housing Code,
and is permitted by or is not prohibited by the Ohio Revised Code and the rules
and regulations of the Ohio Board of Building Standards.
   (e)   To conduct such hearings, in addition to those required by this
Building and Housing Code, to make or cause to be made such investigations and
tests, and to require from other City departments, employees, boards and
commissions such information, as the Board may deem necessary or desirable to
assist in the discharge of any duty or in the exercise of any power mentioned
in this section or elsewhere in this Building and Housing Code.
   (f)   In a specific case, to hear an appeal for authorization of variations
in the requirements of this Building and Housing Code, where such variations
are permitted to be made by the Board under the provisions of this Building and
Housing Code, provided that such appeals are filed as required in Section
1424.04(b) for appealing a decision of the Superintendent.
   In matters to be acted upon by the Board, over which other departments or
divisions of the City government, in addition to the Division of Building and
Zoning Inspection, have jurisdiction, the director of the department or the
head of the division having such jurisdiction shall be consulted before such
matters are finally acted upon by the Board.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1424.04 APPEALS FROM SUPERINTENDENT’S DECISION; PROCEDURE; FEES.
   (a)   Any decision of the Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection
made in the enforcement of this Building and Housing Code may be appealed to
the Board of Zoning and Building Appeals by any person adversely affected by
such decision.
   (b)   An appeal shall be perfected by the appellant filing with the
Superintendent a notice of his or her intention to appeal, and a recital of the
decision appealed and the appellant’s exceptions thereto, together with a fee
of two hundred dollars ($200.00), payable to the City, to be deposited in the
Trust Account. Upon receipt of such notice and other matter herein required,
the Superintendent shall, within seven business days thereafter, transmit to
the members of the Board a copy of the notice of appeal, the recital of the
decision appealed and of the appellant’s exceptions thereto, together with a
statement by the Superintendent of his or her reasons for such decision.
   (c)   The appellant may, at his or her own expense, be represented at the
hearing of his or her appeal by counsel and by any experts on the question
appealed, whom he or she may select. The Board shall have the authority to call
in such other persons for testimony as it sees fit.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81; Ord. 75-1985. Passed 1-13-86.)
1424.05 PUBLIC HEARING REQUIRED.
   The requirement that the Board of Zoning and Building Appeals shall hold a
public hearing on each appeal is mandated by Section
6.03C. of the City Charter.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)

1426.01 PERMIT REQUIRED PRIOR TO COMMENCING WORK; NONCOMPLIANCE; REMEDIES.
   (a)   No person shall commence any work for which a permit is required until
such permit has been issued by the proper official and all fees paid.
   (b)   If it is found that any person is in violation of any provision of
this Building and Housing Code or any other ordinance requiring a permit, the
Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection shall issue a stop work order.
The owner and/or contractor named in such stop work order shall cease all
further work on the building or structure placed under a stop work order until
such time as all requirements of this Building and Housing Code or any other
ordinance listed in the order which is being violated have been resolved to the
satisfaction of the Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection or any
other official charged with the responsibility of enforcing this or any
applicable ordinances.
   (c)   The Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection and the Director
of Public Service are hereby authorized to request that the Department of Law
begin proceedings in a Summit County court to obtain an injunction to halt any
work for which a stop work order has been issued if the owner and/or contractor
has willfully failed to comply with said stop work order.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1426.02 SPECIFIC PERMITS REQUIRED; EXCEPTION.
   (a)   Required Permits. A separate permit is required to commence or proceed
with each operation regulated by or included under the provisions of this
Building and Housing Code, as follows:
      (1)   To construct or erect a building or structure;
      (2)   To construct or erect an addition to an existing building;
      (3)   To erect, re-erect, place, hang or in any manner display a sign or
outdoor advertising display, except when the same is on the inside of a
building or is excepted under the provisions of Section
1454.02;
      (4)   To make major alterations in or on a building or structure;
      (5)   To repair the structural parts of a building or structure;
      (6)   To erect or install amusement devices;
      (7)   To install an automatic sprinkler system;
      (8)   To erect a chimney, smokestack or flue, when not included in a
permit for a building or structure;
      (9)   To install electric wiring and fixtures;
      (10)   To install elevator or escalator equipment;
      (11)   To erect a fire escape, when not included in a permit for a
building;
      (12)   To install refrigeration and air conditioning equipment;
      (13)   To install forced or gravity warm air equipment;
      (14)   To construct a foundation in advance of a superstructure;
      (15)   To erect a marquee or canopy;
      (16)   To move a building;
      (17)   To install plumbing, plumbing fixtures, sewers and drains;
      (18)   To raise a building;
      (19)   To raze or wreck a building;
      (20)   To recover the exterior sides of the walls of a building with
anything other than a liquid protective material;
      (21)   To construct a retaining wall whose top will be more than three
feet above the adjoining grade;
      (22)   To install sidewalk elevators or lifts;
      (23)   To install a stoker;
      (24)   To erect a tent of more than 360 square feet of ground area
contained;
      (25)   To construct a vault under a sidewalk;
      (26)   To install ventilating systems; and
      (27)   To occupy a portion of a roadway or a street.
   A permit is required for fences over eight feet high, and for fences five
feet high or higher which surround swimming pools or the lot upon which a
swimming pool is located, as provided in Section
1456.02. A permit shall also be required to erect, install, repair or alter any
other structure, appliance or device for which a permit fee is required by this
Building and Housing Code.
   (b)   Exception. Manufacturing companies that maintain a permanent
engineering department for the design and regular inspection of elevators shall
not be required to secure permits for the installation of elevators on their
own property as provided for in subsection (a) hereof. Companies qualifying
under this exception must first file a written statement with the
Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection, stating their intention to
maintain such a department and naming the engineers who are to be responsible
for such installation and inspections.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1426.03 PERMIT APPLICATION; FORM AND CONTENTS.
   (a)   An application to the Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection
for a permit shall be submitted in such form as the Superintendent may
prescribe.
   (b)   The application shall be made in writing by the owner or the lessee,
or an agent of either, or the architect, engineer or builder employed in
connection with the proposed work.
   (c)   The application shall contain the full names and addresses of the
owner and the contractor, and of the officer in charge if the owner is a
corporate body.
   (d)   The application shall contain the estimated cost, including material,
labor and planning costs, as well as all related costs, for which a permit is
requested. If an applicant for a permit fails to give a correct statement of
cost of the work for which a permit is requested, the Superintendent may submit
such work to the Board of Zoning and Building Appeals for an estimate as
determined by the majority of its members. Such estimate as the Board may so
determine shall be used in the granting of the permit.
   (e)   The application shall describe briefly the proposed work and shall
give such additional information as may be required by the Superintendent for
an intelligent understanding of the proposed work.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1426.04 PERMIT INFORMATION.
   (a)   When applying for a building permit, an applicant shall:
      (1)   Furnish the house number.
      (2)   Furnish the lot number and the name of the allotment and other
legal identification.
      (3)   Furnish a scaled plot plan showing the size of the lot and the
location of the buildings on the lot.
      (4)   Show how roof water is disposed of.
      (5)   Furnish a basement plan showing the thickness of walls, the
location of the furnace, the center post footings and other footings, and the
size of the chimney.
      (6)   Furnish a complete set of floor plans.
      (7)   Furnish at least two elevations on plans.
      (8)   Furnish a complete set of framing plans, showing the size and
spacing of joists, the size of beams, etc.
      (9)   Know between what cross streets the building is to be located.
      (10)   Furnish a heating layout and heat loss plan.
      (11)   Furnish an electric layout, including service placement.
   (b)   An applicant shall agree to permit conditions specified in Section
1426.13.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1426.05 SUBMISSION OF SPECIFICATIONS AND PLANS; REFERENCE TO CODE COMPLIANCE.
   (a)   Two copies of specifications and of plans and elevations, drawn to
scale, with sufficient clarity and detail to show the use of parts of the
building or structure and compliance with this Building and Housing Code and
other pertinent laws and ordinances, shall accompany every application, except
that the Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection may, at his or her
discretion, modify or waive this requirement when it is evident that the work
can, because of its character or triviality, be sufficiently described in an
application.
   (b)   When this Building and Housing Code or any other ordinance or law is
referred to on a plan or in a specification, a general expression to the effect
that the work shall be done or that the plans or specifications shall be
carried out to the satisfaction or approval of the Superintendent, or in
accordance with this Building and Housing Code or other ordinances or laws,
shall not be used. Reference may be made on a plan or in a specification to a
section or subsection of this Building and Housing Code or other ordinances or
laws, by the number of the section or subsection, but if such section or
subsection contains more than one subject or part therein, such section or
subsection referred to shall be quoted in full.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1426.06 PLOT PLAN.
   A plot plan submitted for a permit to build shall contain the following
information:
   (a)   The elevation of the first floor of the dwelling, or attached garages
or unattached garages, and other accessory buildings;
   (b)   The finish curb or crown elevation of the street at the point of
extension of the lot line;
   (c)   The finish grade elevation at each principal corner of the structure;
   (d)   The finish grade elevation at both sides of abrupt changes of grade,
such as retaining walls, slope, etc.;
   (e)   Other elevations that may be necessary to show grading and drainage;
   (f)   The sewer grade and elevation as approved by the Public Service
Department or the City Engineer;
   (g)   A scale of the plot plan, which shall not be less than one inch equals
twenty feet;
   (h)   The lot, lot number and allotment or other legal identification;
   (i)   The dimensions of the plot and the north point;
   (j)   The dimensions of the front or building lines, and rear and side
yards;
   (k)   The location and dimensions of garages, carports and other accessory
buildings;
   (l)   The location of walks, driveways and approaches;
   (m)   The location of steps, terraces, porches, fences and retaining walls;
   (n)   The locations and dimensions of easements, if any;
   (o)   The location, the width of streets and rights of way and the types of
street surfaces; and
   (p)   Proposed drainage and curb cuts as approved by the Public Service
Department or the City Engineer.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1426.07 PLAN SUPPLEMENTS AND ADDITIONAL DATA.
   (a)   The Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection may require
details, computations, stress diagrams and other data necessary to describe the
construction and basis of calculations. He or she may also require plans
showing the location of the proposed building or structure and of every
existing building or structure on the site or lot, in accordance with a
boundary line survey prepared by a registered surveyor.
   (b)   For other than dwellings and minor buildings, the Superintendent shall
require that the unit stresses and live loads used in the design of the
building be tabulated on the structural drawings, and that the drawings bear a
statement by the designer certifying that the unit stresses, permitted by this
Building and Housing Code, have not been exceeded. He or she shall require
structural plans and computations to bear the signature of the registered
architect or registered engineer in charge of the structural design.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1426.08 APPLICATION OR PLAN AMENDMENTS; SUPPLEMENTARY PERMIT.
   Nothing in this chapter shall prohibit the filing of amendments to an
application or to a plan or other record accompanying the same at any time
before the change is made on the job, in the work for which the permit was
sought. Such amendments, after approval by the Superintendent of Building and
Zoning Inspection, shall be filed with and be deemed a part of the original
application, except that an application covering the proposed change shall be
submitted and a supplementary permit shall be obtained if the nature of the
change makes a supplementary permit necessary.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1426.09 APPLICATION TIME LIMIT; ABANDONED APPLICATIONS.
   An application for a permit for any proposed work shall be deemed to have
been abandoned six months after the date of filing, unless a permit has been
issued before then. After an application has been abandoned, the Superintendent
of Building and Zoning Inspection may destroy and dispose of all records, plans
and specifications submitted in connection with the application.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1426.10 APPLICATION AND PLAN EXAMINATION; APPROVAL.
   The Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection shall examine, or cause
to be examined, each application for a permit and the plans, specifications and
computations which may be submitted therewith, and it shall be determined by
such examination whether the matter mentioned in the application and indicated,
described and determined in the plans, specifications and computations, is in
accord with the requirements of this Building and Housing Code and all other
pertinent laws and ordinances. However, if the plans and specifications
submitted for approval bear the seal of a registered architect or of a
registered engineer, showing that a responsible person has prepared or
supervised the preparation of the plans and specifications, the Superintendent
may accept the plans and specifications, certified by the architect or
engineer, as complying with the requirements of this Building and Housing Code
pertaining to design loads, stresses, strains, strengths and stability. If the
Superintendent is satisfied that the plans and other matter submitted therewith
conform to the requirements of this Building and Housing Code and other
pertinent laws and ordinances, he or she shall endorse in writing, or stamp,
both sets of plans "Approved", and such approval shall bear the signature of
the employee of the Division of Building and Zoning Inspection who checked the
plans and other matter submitted therewith.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1426.11 COMPLETION OF EXISTING BUILDINGS.
   Nothing in this Building and Housing Code shall require changes in plans,
construction or designated use of a building for which a lawful permit has been
previously issued or which has been otherwise lawfully authorized, and the
construction of which has been actually begun within ninety days after this
Building and Housing Code becomes effective, provided that the entire building
shall be complete as authorized within two years thereafter.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1426.12 PERMIT ISSUANCE OR REFUSAL.
   (a)   If the Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection is satisfied
that the work described in an application for a permit conforms to the
requirements of this Building and Housing Code and other pertinent laws and
ordinances, and if the plans and other matter submitted in connection therewith
have been approved as required in Section
1426.10, he or she shall issue a permit therefor to the applicant, provided
that the Director of Public Service shall be promptly advised of all permits
issued for moving or razing buildings.
   (b)   If the application for a permit or the plans or other matter filed
therewith describes or indicates work which does not conform to the
requirements of this Building and Housing Code or other pertinent laws or
ordinances, the Superintendent shall not issue a permit, but he or she shall
notify the applicant of such refusal and give the reasons therefor. Such
refusal and reasons shall, when requested by the applicant, be in writing. All
plans and specifications filed with the application shall be returned to the
applicant if called for at the Division of Building and Zoning Inspection
within thirty days after the date of the refusal of the permit.
   (c)   The Superintendent shall act upon plans and applications in the order
received and without unnecessary delay.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1426.13 PERMIT CONDITIONS AND RIGHTS; SITE MARKERS AND COMMENCING WORK; LOT
REVISION.
   (a)   All work performed under a permit issued by the Superintendent of
Building and Zoning Inspection shall confirm to the approved application and
plans, and approved amendments thereof, except as provided in subsection (b)
hereof.
   (b)   A permit shall be construed to be a license to proceed with the work
described therein and shall not be construed as authority to violate, cancel,
alter or set aside any of the provisions of this Building and Housing Code, nor
shall the issuance of a permit prevent the Superintendent thereafter from
requiring a correction of errors in plans or in construction, or of violations
of this Building and Housing Code. A building permit carries with it the right
to install any crane, derrick, material elevator, material or office shed in a
safe manner, which may be required for temporary use during the erection of the
building, except it does not carry the right to use any portion of a street,
roadway or any other public property.
   (c)   Any issued permit becomes invalid unless the work authorized by it
shall be commenced within ninety days after its issuance, or if the work
authorized by such permit is suspended or abandoned for a period of three
months or more after the time the work is commenced. "Commenced", as used
herein, means any work initiated for which a permit has been issued and plans
therefor have been approved. However, for good cause, an extension of time not
to exceed ninety days may be allowed, in writing, by the Superintendent when
applied for by the person to whom the permit was issued. The request for an
extension of time shall be filed prior to the expiration of the initial permit.
Only one such extension shall be granted.
   (d)   Before any work for which a permit is required is started on a new
building or on an addition to an existing building, all boundary line
intersections of the site, where the building or addition is to be located,
shall be marked with permanent markers, except that if it is not possible to
maintain such markers during construction, accurately located offset markers
may be used. All markers shall be set so as to be readily located at any time
during the construction of the building or structure.
   (e)   All buildings hereafter constructed shall be set at elevations which
will facilitate proper surface water drainage.
      (1)   The established sidewalk grade shall be shown on all applications
to build, where required by the Public Service Department or the City Engineer.
      (2)   The sewer grade and elevation shall be shown on all applications to
build, where required by the Public Service Department or the City Engineer.
      (3)   Where no sanitary sewer is available at a building site or lot, the
building application shall be approved by the Department of Health, showing
that the site is suitable for the installation of a septic tank and leaching
device, or such sanitary installations as are deemed necessary.
   (f)   The location of all new construction or additions to existing
construction as shown on the approved plot diagram or an approved amendment
thereof, shall be strictly adhered to.
   (g)   No person shall reduce or diminish the area of a lot or plot of which
a plot diagram has been filed and used as the basis for a permit, unless a
revised plot diagram showing the proposed change in conditions shall have been
filed and approved by the Superintendent. However, this does not apply when the
lot is reduced by reason of a street opening or widening or other improvement.
   (h)   The issuance of a building permit shall constitute a certificate of
qualification for the named contractor and/or owner. Revocation, suspension or
refusal to issue a building permit shall be as specified in Section
1428.24.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1426.14 PERMIT FORMS AND INFORMATION RECORDED THEREON.
   (a)   The forms for a permit issued by the Superintendent of Building and
Zoning Inspection shall consist of a permit and a permit card and shall be such
as may be prescribed by the Superintendent.
   (b)   The permit shall contain the name of the owner and the contractor and
shall describe briefly the work covered by the permit and shall give such
additional information as the Superintendent may require for office and
inspection purposes. Such information shall be consistent with that shown on
the application.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1426.15 FORM OR SIGNATURE OF ISSUING AUTHORITY.
   Every permit issued by the Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection
under the provisions of this Building and Housing Code shall have his or her
name or signature affixed thereto.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1426.16 PERMITS FOR WORK REQUIRING SPECIAL SUPERVISION.
   Whenever the work covered by a permit involves construction under conditions
which, in the opinion of the Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection,
are hazardous or complex, or for other good reason required special
supervision, the Superintendent may require that the architect or engineer who
affixed his or her seal to, or who made the plans or computations, shall
supervise such work, be responsible for its conformity with the approved plans,
and forthwith, upon its completion, make and file with the Superintendent a
written certification that the work has been done in conformity with the
approved plans and with the structural requirements of this Building and
Housing Code. If any architect or engineer is not available for such
supervision and certification, the owner of the building or structure in
question shall employ, in his or her stead, another architect or engineer.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1426.17 SPECIAL PERMITS AND APPROVALS FROM OTHER CITY AUTHORITIES.
   (a)   The Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection shall not issue a
permit or certificate for the occupancy, construction or removal of any
building or structure in connection with a business or operation which required
a permit or approval from Council or from any other City department or
division, until the applicant presents written evidence, satisfactory to the
Superintendent, that all such required approvals or permits have been obtained.
   (b)   Special permits as required include, but are not limited to, permits
for moving buildings over streets, occupation of streets for construction
purposes, sidewalk construction on public property, pavement openings for any
purpose, cutting holes through curbing for roof drain outlets, cutting curbing
for driveways, water and sewer tap-in fees and inspections, permits to work in
the City right-of-way, topography review for construction and filling/grading
of properties, rapid access key box requirements for emergency situations and
as required by
Chapter 1437 or as required by the fire code official.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81; Ord. 69-2005. Passed 10-11-05.)
1426.18 PERMITS FOR PARTS OF BUILDINGS.
   Nothing in this Building and Housing Code shall be construed to prevent the
Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection from issuing a permit for the
construction of a part of a building or structure before the entire plans and
detailed statements of the building or structure have been submitted or
approved, if adequate information and detailed statements have been presented
for the same and have been found to comply with this Building and Housing Code.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1426.19 PERMITS FOR BUILDINGS TO BE REMOVED OR RAZED.
   The Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection shall be given not less
than forty-eight hours after the filing of an application for a permit, to move
or raze a building, to inspect such building and adjoining buildings and
structures. If he or she finds that the work can be executed safely in the
manner proposed and that the resulting conditions will not violate any of the
provisions of this Building and Housing Code or other City ordinances, he or
she shall issue a permit therefor upon such conditions that he or she deems
best for the preservation of public safety.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1426.20 PERMIT TIME LIMITATION AND EXPIRATION; FEE APPLIED TO NEW PERMIT.
   A permit under which no work is commenced within ninety days shall expire as
provided for in Section
1426.13(c). The fee for a permit which has expired and under which no work has
been or will be done shall not be refunded, but such fee may be applied toward
a new permit for the same applicant, at the same or a different location, if
the new permit is applied for and issued within three months after the issuance
of the expired or unused permit, provided the permit receipt, permit and/or
permit card for the expired or unused permit is returned to the Division of
Building and Zoning Inspection.
   This section applies to any type of permit authorized to be issued by the
Division of Building and Zoning Inspection.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1426.21 PLANS TO BE KEPT AT SITE.
   One set of approved plans shall be returned to the applicant when the permit
is issued for the work indicated on the plans. This set of plans shall be kept
at the site of the work and shall be available for examination by the
Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection or his or her authorized
representative at all reasonable times.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1426.22 POSTING AND DISPLAY OF PERMIT CARD AT WORK SITE.
   (a)   No operations requiring a permit shall be commenced until the permit
card therefor is posted in a conspicuous place, near the front of the premises
and in such position as to permit the inspectors of the Division of Building
and Zoning Inspection to make the required entries thereon regarding inspection
work. The card shall be preserved and remain posted until the completion of the
work for which it was issued.
   (b)   No person shall remove or cover such permit card until the work for
which the card was issued has been approved by the Superintendent of Building
and Zoning Inspection.
   (c)   It shall be the duty of the Chief of Police to notify the
Superintendent of every location where work has commenced or is being performed
and a permit card, when required by this Building and Housing Code, is not
found by an officer of the Division of Police to be displayed or posted at such
location. The Chief of Police shall give such assistance to the Superintendent
as may be lawful and necessary to cause such work, for which a required permit
has not been procured, to be discontinued until a permit is displayed or posted
as required by this Building and Housing Code.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1426.23 STREET AND SIDEWALK OBSTRUCTION PERMIT; BOND, FEE AND RESTORATION
DEPOSIT.
   (a)   Permits for occupying portions of sidewalks and roadways for building
operations shall be issued by the Director of Public Service. Before such
permit is granted, the Director shall prepare an estimate of the cost of
restoring the sidewalk and roadway to a condition as good as before occupation.
The applicant for the permit shall comply with the following conditions:
      (1)   File with the Director of Public Service a bond, when the Director
deems it necessary or desirable, in an amount to be designated by him or her,
but in no case less than five thousand dollars ($5,000), to indemnify and keep
the City harmless from any and all loss, cost, expense or liability of any kind
whatever which it may suffer or be put to, or which may be recovered from it by
reason of the issuance of such permit, or any act or thing done or neglected to
be done under or by virtue of the authority given in such permit, and the
requirements of this Building and Housing Code.
      (2)   Pay an occupation permit fee of one dollar ($1.00) per month, or
fraction thereof, for each 100 square feet or fraction thereof of sidewalk or
roadway space, covering the period for which the permit is to be issued.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
      (3)   Deposit in cash the estimated cost of restoring the sidewalk and
roadway, which in no case shall be less than two dollars ($2.00) per square
foot. If the required deposit exceeds one thousand dollars ($1,000), a good and
sufficient surety company bond may be furnished for the amount in excess
thereof. The surety bond shall be liable to the City for all expenses of
restoration in excess of one thousand dollars ($1,000). The cash deposit shall
be presented to the Director of Finance for deposit in the Trust Account.
(Ord. 108-1989. Passed 1-8-90.)
   (b)   The period for which the permit is issued may be extended by the
Director of Public Service upon payment by the applicant of additional
occupation fees.
   (c)   Any obstruction permit issued under the terms of this Building and
Housing Code may be revoked by the Director of Public Service at any time.
   (d)   When a permittee has relinquished the space occupied and restored the
sidewalk and roadway to the satisfaction of the Director of Public Service, the
Director of Public Service shall issue a certificate to the Director of Finance
to this effect, and the Director of Finance shall thereupon forthwith issue a
check for the amount deposited into the Trust Account for this purpose.
However, if the permittee fails to restore the same within five days after the
completion of the building or structure for which the deposit was required,
then the Director of Public Service shall have the right to use so much of the
amount deposited as will be necessary to remove all obstructions and to restore
the sidewalk and roadway to a condition as good as they were before occupation,
and the amount thus expended shall be deducted from the amount of the deposit.
However, nothing contained herein shall preclude the City from maintaining an
action against the permittee to recover for damage done to any sidewalk or
roadway.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1426.24 DEPOSIT FOR STREET CLEANING; NONCOMPLIANCE; RETURN OF DEPOSIT.
   (a)   Any person who obtains a building permit in the City for new
construction for a dwelling and/or a commercial or industrial structure, shall
post with the Director of Finance a security cash bond in the sum of one
hundred dollars ($100.00) to assure no littering of streets, roads or public
ways with mud and/or other building materials. A security deposit shall be
posted for each building permit.
   Any person who obtains a building permit and contemplates more than one
building permit in any subdivision or subdivisions that are adjacent,
contiguous and adjoining each other in one development, is hereby granted the
alternative of posting with the Director of Finance a cash bond in the amount
of five hundred dollars ($500.00) in lieu of the cash bond in the amount of one
hundred dollars ($100.00) for each building permit. However, in the event it is
necessary for the City to use such security deposit as set forth in subsection
(b) hereof, the Director shall notify the person who posted such bond in the
amount of five hundred dollars ($500.00) as to the amount of money used by the
City, and, within five days, such person shall reimburse the City the sum of
money used in order to maintain the cash bond in the total sum of five hundred
dollars ($500.00). If such charges are not paid within the allotted time, the
Division of Building and Zoning Inspection is hereby ordered not to issue any
additional permits for the development covered by the reduced bond until such
time as payment is made.
(Ord. 100-1971. Passed 12-13-71; Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
   (b)   Any person who causes or permits the littering of streets, roads or
other public ways with debris or excavating materials by reason of the removal
or conveyance of such materials on the streets, roads or other public ways,
shall clean and/or remove such debris within twenty-four hours after being
notified by the Director of Public Service or his or her authorized agent. If
the person fails to remove or is unable to remove such materials, then such
cleaning service shall be rendered by the Department of Public Service at the
current hourly rates of its equipment and personnel.
   The Department of Public Service shall render the bill for such services to
the person and shall also send a duplicate bill to the Director of Finance. In
the event the person does not pay such bill within five days from the date of
such bill, then the Director is authorized to use the security deposit for the
payment of such bill.
   (c)   The Director of Finance is hereby authorized to return the security
deposit or any unused portion thereof when the Superintendent of Building and
Zoning Inspection issues a certificate of occupancy.
(Ord. 29-1970. Passed 3-9-70; Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1426.25 PERMIT FOR USE OF EXPLOSIVES, BLASTING AND OTHER HAZARDOUS OPERATIONS;
PERMIT AND SUPERVISION FEES.
   (a)   No dynamite or other explosive containing nitroglycerine as a
component part thereof shall be kept for sale or stored in any place within the
City. No person, except as otherwise provided herein, shall use, discharge or
cause to be discharged or exploded within the City any black powder, dynamite
or other explosive for blasting operations without first obtaining a permit
therefor from the Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection who shall
make and enforce rules and regulations for the handling and use of such
explosives within the City.
   (b)   Only a competent and experienced blaster shall obtain a permit, which
shall be valid only for the particular operation for which it is granted.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
   (c)   The fee for a permit to blast shall be one hundred dollars ($100.00)
and the permit shall be obtained from the Division of Building and Zoning
Inspection, subject to supervision by the Fire Division. The services of the
supervising inspector overseeing the operation shall be paid by the applicant,
at the rate of twenty-five dollars ($25.00) per man-hour, when the services are
rendered in the course of a normal day's work schedule, which is 8:00 a.m. to
4:00 p.m., Monday through Friday. If performed on a holiday or at any other
time which is not normal working hours, the fee shall be increased one and one-
half times.
(Ord. 108-1989. Passed 1-8-90.)
   (d)   When, in the opinion of the Fire Chief, a hazardous condition exists
due to the applicant's operation, the normal building permit shall be obtained
and a full-time inspector retained and the City reimbursed in accordance with
subsection (c) hereof.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1426.26 REINSPECTION FEE; PENALTIES; AFTER HOURS INSPECTIONS; NO INSPECTION
UNTIL FEES ARE PAID.
   (a)   Reinspection. The fee for a reinspection shall be forty dollars
($40.00) per additional trip and shall be paid in advance. A reinspection is
necessary for reasons of incompetence, incomplete or negligent work.
(Ord. 108-1989. Passed 1-8-90; Ord. 69-2002. Passed 11-12-02.)
   (b)   Penalties.
      (1)   All fees for permits to be charged by virtue of any ordinance
governing buildings and structures, this Building and Housing Code or any other
code, either in their present form or an amended form, shall be subject to an
increase of 200 percent if the work for which the permit is required is
commenced before the permit is issued or before written consent of the
Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection is procured, which increase
shall be collected by the Superintendent before the issuance of such permit.
      (2)   A penalty of seventy-five dollars ($75.00) per notification will be
charged for occupancy prior to final approval. Notification fees can be
assessed no more than once every seven calendar days.
      (3)   Nothing in this section shall be construed to repeal or modify any
other section of any other ordinance providing for penalties, and the penalty
provided herein shall be in addition to any other such penalty.
   (c)   After Hours Inspections. An inspection will be made at other than
normal hours (8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday), when requested by
an owner or contractor during normal hours and deemed necessary by the
Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection for efficient and effective
construction of such project, provided a minimum fee of two hundred dollars
($200.00) is paid in advance for each inspection requested, which fee shall be
in addition to all other applicable fees.
   (d)   No Inspection Until Fees Paid. An inspection or reinspection will not
be made until all fees are paid.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81; Ord. 69-2002. Passed 11-12-02.)
1426.27 OWNER-REQUESTED INSPECTIONS.
   (a)   An owner, or his or her authorized agent, may request, in writing,
that an inspection be made of his or her premises when no remodeling, additions
or improvements are contemplated. Requests should be addressed to the
Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
   (b)   Fees are based upon one inspector spending no more than one hour of
cumulative time. Fees for such an inspection as listed below must accompany the
request and are as follows:
   Type   Fee
   Building or structure inspection   $50.00
   Heating inspection
   (does not include smoke testing of furnaces)   50.00
   Electrical inspection   50.00
   Special commercial inspection (+3%)   50.00
(Ord. 69-2002. Passed 11-12-02.)
1426.28 CERTIFICATES OF OCCUPANCY.
   The requirements for certificates of occupancy shall be as provided for in
the Zoning Code of the City.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1426.29 CERTIFICATES FOR COMPLETED STRUCTURES.
   Upon the completion and approval of the construction, alteration or repair
of a structure, the Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection shall, if
so requested by the permit holder, issue a certificate in the effect that the
structure has been completed in conformity with the provisions of this Building
and Housing Code, and also indicating the use or uses to which the structure
may thereafter be put and to what extent.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1426.30 CERTIFICATES FOR COMPLETED INSTALLATIONS.
   When a certificate is specifically required by a provision of this Building
and Housing Code for an installation, extension, alteration or repair of an
elevator or elevator equipment, plumbing, electric wiring or a heating system,
no person shall use or permit the use of the installation, equipment or
appliance to which such provision applies, until the appropriate certificate
has been issued.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1426.31 PLANS EXAMINER; ALTERNATE PLANS EXAMINER; REIMBURSEMENT FOR SERVICES
FOR PLANS EXAMINATION.
   (a)   The Director of Public Service is hereby authorized to contract with
an individual who meets the requirements of the Ohio Building Code and has been
certified by the Ohio Board of Building Standards as a Plan Examiner for
structures that are governed by the Ohio Building Code.
   (b)   The Director of Public Service is hereby authorized to contract with
an individual who meets the requirements of the Ohio Building Code as an
alternate Plans Examiner. He or she shall only be used when the Plans Examiner
provided for in subsection (a) hereof is not available to approve plans
submitted under the Ohio Building Code.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
   (c)   (1)   An applicant for a building permit who requests approval of
plans for a structure that is governed by the Ohio Building Code shall
reimburse the City for the total cost of the plans examination.
      (2)   There shall be a minimum fee of sixty dollars ($60.00) payable when
plans are presented for examination and approval.
      (3)   If the fee charged for the examination exceeds the minimum fee for
examination, the applicant shall pay the additional amount at the time the
building permit is issued, along with all lawful charges provided by ordinance
for said permit.
1426.32 PERMIT FEES; BUILDINGS AND STRUCTURES; PENALTY.
   No permit for which a fee is required by any ordinance shall be issued until
the applicant for the permit has paid to the Superintendent of Building and
Zoning Inspection, or to the person otherwise designated by ordinance, the fee
hereinafter prescribed. Fees shall be calculated to the nearest multiple of
five cents ($.05).
   Each applicant for a permit shall make a sworn statement or affirmation, in
writing, setting forth, in accordance with a bona fide estimate, the total
value of the proposed building, structure, addition, alteration, repair or
installation, including the cost of any and all plumbing, electrical, heating
and other mechanical equipment, devices, appliances, materials, etc., which
will be incorporated therein, and also the value of all labor, regardless of
who is to do the work or make the installations.
   All area and perimeter measurements shall be made on the exterior of
structure surfaces.

installation and the fee for a permit for an addition, alteration or repair to

contained herein.

   A bond shall be filed with the Director of Public Service in the amount of
one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000) before the moving of a building by a
permittee. The conditions of such bond shall be that the owner of the building
and the person actually carrying out the work of moving the building shall
comply with all the general laws of Ohio and City ordinances in the moving of
the building, and, further, that they will indemnify and keep the City harmless
from all damages, liabilities, claims, losses, costs or judgments, made or
rendered against or suffered by the City because of such moving operations.
However, in lieu of the bond, a public liability and property damage insurance
policy, issued by a solvent insurance company, in the amount of five hundred
thousand dollars ($500,000), may be deposited with the Director of Public
Service, provided that the City shall be indemnified by reason of any losses
sustained by reason of the liability imposed by law upon the City on account of
such moving operations, and provided, further that the moving contractor shall
also be responsible and pay for all damage caused to the streets, overhead
wires, trees and other objects which may be lawfully placed or which lawfully
exist in the streets. No building or moving permit shall be issued except with
the approval of the City Engineer for the construction, alteration or
relocation of any building or structure within or adjacent to the right-of-way
limits of any limited or controlled-access highway project or other highway
project.
   No person shall knowingly make or cause to be made, either directly or
indirectly or through any agency whatsoever, any false or fraudulent statement,
or knowingly fail to disclose information to the City or any of its officers,
agents, employees or departments, with the intent that such statement or
omission shall be relied upon to cause the issuance of a building or moving
permit for the construction, alteration or relocation of any building or
structure within or adjacent to the right-of-way limits of any limited or
controlled-access highway project, grade separation project or other highway
project.
   In addition to the above mentioned fee for moving a building on or across a
public street or public alley, a permit fee shall be paid to the Division of
Building and Zoning Inspection as follows: For a foundation with no basement at
the new location for buildings moved over a public street or alley, the fee
shall be as provided in subsection (f) hereof. When a basement is to be
provided at the new location, the fee for the permit for the new basement,
including the foundation, shall be at the same rate as is provided in this
section for an addition.

1426.35 ENGINEERING PLANS REVIEW FEES.
   (a)   Fees Required. Any person desiring to obtain a plans review by the
Municipal Engineer under the provisions of this section shall first pay the fee
as required herein to the City. The fees required under this section are in
addition to any permit or building plans fees required elsewhere and shall
include the preliminary, improvement and final plat reviews by the Municipal
Engineer.
   (b)   Municipal Engineer Plans Review Fees.
      (1)   Single-family house building site plans review: $200.00.
      (2)   Multi-family building site plans review:
         A.   First 1,000 square feet of space: $200.00.
         B.   Each additional 1,000 square feet or fraction thereof: $35.00.
         C.   One-half of payment is due prior to review of plans, other half
is due upon plans approval.
      (3)   Subdivision lots plans review:
         A.   First 50 lots: $100.00 per lot.
         B.   Each additional lot after first 50 lots: $50.00 per lot.
         C.   One-half of payment is due prior to review of plans, other half
is due upon plans approval.
      (4)   Commercial or industrial building site plans review:
         A.   First 1,000 square feet of a building: $200.00.
         B.   Each additional 1,000 square feet or fraction thereof: $35.00.
         C.   One-half of payment is due prior to review of plans, other half
is due upon plans approval.
   (c)   Costs for Additional Work. Any additional work performed or extra
costs incurred by any City department shall be added to the application fee and
the applicant shall bear all additional expenses in connection with the matter
contained in an application. The additional work performed or extra costs may
include, but is not limited to, engineering, architectural, or other
professional services.
   (d)   In addition to the established Municipal Engineer plans review fees
listed in the previous subsections, the Director of Public Service may
authorize and approve a reasonable increase in those fees once per year,
beginning after January 1, 2006. No annual increase shall exceed 3%.
(Ord. 3-2005. Passed 2-28-05.)

1428.01 REGISTRATION REQUIRED.
   For the purpose of this chapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   (a)   "Contractor." Any person or entity who contracts or is employed to
perform any work involved in construction. The person or entity purchasing may
be the owner, occupant or resident agent of the premises or another contractor.
The term "contractor" excludes a person who is an employee of the purchasing
person or entity. The phrase "work which requires a permit" includes, but is
not limited to, the following: building, plumbing, electrical heating,
ventilating, air conditioning, sheet metal piping, sewer, signs, refrigeration,
cement, asphalt, masonry, excavating, carpentry, drywall roofing, structural
steel siding installation or sprinkler installation.
   (b)   "General Contractor." A contractor as defined in division (a) hereof
who contracts with the owner, occupant or resident agent of the premises.
   (c)   "Subcontractor." A contractor who contracts with a general contractor
or other subcontractor, but who does not contract directly with the owner,
occupant, of resident agent.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81; Ord. 71-2002. Passed 11-12-02; Ord. 56-2005.
Passed 10-24-05.)
