1436.01 APPLIANCES REQUIRED FOR BUILDINGS OTHER THAN DWELLINGS.
   All buildings, other than dwellings, shall be equipped with fire-
extinguishing appliances conforming to the provisions of this chapter, the Ohio
Building Code and the Fire Prevention Code.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1436.02 INSTALLATION STANDARDS.
   Approved fire-extinguishing equipment, installed in accordance with
standards set forth in the Ohio Building Code, Section 4101:2-9, shall be
deemed to conform to the provisions of this chapter, unless inconsistent with
the provisions, intent and purpose of this Building and Housing Code or the
rules and regulations of the Summit County Department of Health.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1436.03 APPROVED APPLIANCES, FITTINGS AND DEVICES.
   Appliances, fittings and devices bearing the label of Underwriters’
Laboratories, Inc., or listed in publications issued by Underwriters’
Laboratories, Inc., may be accepted as conforming to the requirements of this
chapter, if not in conflict with standards established by the Ohio Building
Code.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1436.04 STANDPIPES REQUIRED.
   Buildings hereafter erected shall be equipped with standpipes and hoses as
follows:
   (a)   Buildings less than fifty feet in height shall not be required to have
standpipes unless required elsewhere in this Building and Housing Code or by
the Ohio Building Code.
   (b)   Buildings fifty to seventy-five feet in height shall have standpipes
not less than four inches in diameter.
   (c)   Buildings exceeding seventy-five feet in height shall have standpipes
not less than six inches in diameter.
   (d)   All occupancies required by the Ohio Building Code to have standpipes
shall have such standpipes.
   (e)   Where permitted by N.F.P.A. Bulletin No. 14, standpipes may be sized
by hydraulic calculations of a registered professional engineer.
   (f)   Pressure maintenance pumps shall be provided in all required
installations as defined in N.F.P.A. 20, paragraph 31e.
   (g)   A standpipe water supply lateral shall be provided with a slow opening
and closing valve, as specified by the City Engineer, to prevent water hammer.
   (h)   All systems shall be equipped with a backflow prevention valve between
the pump and the water main, when, by reason of occupancy, there is a potential
for contamination of the potable water supply.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1436.05 STANDPIPE CONNECTION THREADS AND CAPS.
   (a)   The thread of all standpipe connections shall be uniform with that
used by the Division of Fire. Substantial caps to protect the threads shall be
provided on each connection.
   (b)   Standpipes shall be equipped in every story with two and one-half inch
hose connections for use by the Fire Division.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1436.06 STANDPIPE TESTING.
   (a)   Upon the completion of a standpipe installation, and at least once
every two years thereafter, every standpipe shall be tested by a testing or
inspection agency approved by the Fire Chief, and a written report of the
result of such test shall be signed by an authorized representative of such
testing or inspection agency and furnished to the Chief within thirty days
after such test is made.
   (b)   The test shall consist of a static pressure test, with all outlets
closed, equivalent to the designed pressure due to the height of the standpipe.
Flow tests shall also be made to prove that the standpipe, line valves, check
valves and Siamese connections are free from obstructions and workable, and
that the fire pump is in good condition.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1436.07 STANDPIPE MAINTENANCE AND USE.
   (a)   In buildings hereafter erected, required standpipes shall be installed
as the construction progresses, in such a way that they are available for use
by the Fire Division to the topmost floor that has been constructed.
   (b)   After the completion of a building hereafter erected and in buildings
heretofore erected, standpipes, and pumps, tanks and other equipment that is
part of the standpipe system, shall be maintained in readiness for use at all
times.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1436.08 SPRINKLER EQUIPMENT REQUIRED.
   In addition to the requirements specified elsewhere in this Building and
Housing Code for automatic sprinkler equipment, in buildings hereafter erected
and in buildings in which the occupancy is changed so as to transfer the
buildings from one class to another, as classified according to occupancy in
the Ohio Building Code, approved automatic sprinkler equipment shall be
installed and maintained as follows:
   (a)   Buildings used for the manufacture, sale or storage of combustible
goods, material or merchandise shall be equipped with approved automatic
sprinkler equipment under conditions as follows:
      (1)   When the building is of Type 1 (fireproof) or Type 2
(noncombustible) construction and the floor area is more than 50,000 square
feet, except that sprinklers need not be provided if the area is subdivided by
fire walls or fire partitions into areas of not more than 50,000 square feet
(area of one floor).
      (2)   When the building is of Type 1 (fireproof) or Type 2
(noncombustible construction and is more than three stories in height.
      (3)   When the building is of other than Type 1 (fireproof) or Type 2
(noncombustible) construction and is more than two stories in height.
   (b)   Except as herein provided, in multiple dwellings over three stories
high, approved automatic sprinkler equipment shall be installed to protect all
public corridors, halls, stairways, passageways and other exitways as may, in
the opinion of the Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection, be
necessary to facilitate safe egress from the building. In such buildings,
automatic sprinkler heads, effective against the spread of fire, shall be
installed in each elevator shaft, clothes chute, paper chute and dumbwaiter
shaft. Sprinkler heads shall be spaced not more than ten feet apart along the
centerline of hallways, corridors and passageways, and at each landing in exit
stairways, or as approved by the Superintendent or the Fire Chief. Not less
than one sprinkler head shall be placed at a position to be most effective, in
all elevator shafts, clothes chutes, paper chutes and dumbwaiter shafts. All
rooms in such buildings used for hazardous purposes, such as for furniture
repairing or for the storage of flammable materials, shall be equipped with an
approved automatic sprinkler system as directed by the Superintendent or the
Chief. Approved sprinkler systems may be omitted in public halls and corridors
when the floor finish is noncombustible or fire retardant and when all doors,
windows, trim, wall and ceiling finishes, including paints, and all decorations
in or along the halls and corridors, are noncombustible.
   (c)   In buildings of hazardous occupancies, approved sprinkler systems
shall be installed as required in Section
1488.01.
   (d)   In garages, approved automatic sprinkler equipment shall be installed
under the following conditions:
      (1)   In garages used for the storage of loaded commercial trucks where
the floor area in one story exceeds 2,000 square feet and the building is of
Type 3 (exterior masonry wall) or Type 4 (frame) construction.
      (2)   In bus garages exceeding two stories in height.
      (3)   In basement or sub-basement garages housing more than three motor
vehicles.
      (4)   In garages located in buildings in which one or more stories or
parts thereof above such garages are occupied for other purposes, when the
garages have a capacity of twenty or more passenger motor vehicles, or are used
as bus terminals for three or more busses, or are used for the storage or
loading of two or more trucks.
   (e)   Sprinkler equipment shall also be provided in buildings other than
herein specified, where, because of the high fire hazard existing or
anticipated, such protection is deemed necessary by the Superintendent or the
Fire Chief and where required by the Fire Prevention Code.
   (f)   Where the nature of the hazard is such that the application of water
is not an effective means of protection or would unduly spread a fire by
flotation, other adequate means of protection shall be provided.
   (g)   In institutional uses which require occupancy for a period of more
than twenty-four hours, such as, but not limited to, nursing homes, rest homes,
homes for the aged, mental nursing homes, convalescent homes, alcoholic nursing
homes, boarding homes for handicapped or feebleminded children, and boarding
homes for children, an automatic fire-extinguishing system shall be installed
throughout the entire building as required by Ohio Building Code Chapter 4101:
2-9, and such system shall be a “Supervised System” conforming to N.F.P.A.
Standard Numbers 71, 72A, 72B, 72C and 72D. Water flow alarms shall also be
interconnected with the fire alarm system as required by Section
1436.14(a).
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1436.09 WATER SUPPLY; STANDPIPE PRESSURE.
   (a)   Standpipes shall be supplied under full pressure from an adequate
water supply or the water supply shall be furnished automatically by the
opening of a hose outlet or by the operation of suitably located thermostats,
except as follows:
      (1)   In buildings having floor areas of less than 2,500 square feet in
which fire- extinguishing equipment is furnished and placed in accordance with
the requirements of the Fire Prevention Code;
      (2)   In sprinklered buildings in which one and one-half inch hose is
connected to the sprinkler risers in each floor area;
      (3)   In buildings which, because of occupancy or type of construction,
do not, in the opinion of the Fire Chief, require constant and automatic water
supply.
      (4)   Nursing homes, rest homes, homes for the aged, mental nursing
homes, convalescent homes, alcoholic nursing homes, boarding homes for
handicapped or feebleminded children, and boarding homes for children, shall
comply with Ohio Basic Building Code, Chapter 4101:2-9.
   (b)   The minimum supply for Class I and Class III service, as defined in
N.F.P.A. Bulletin No. 14, shall be sufficient to provide 500 gallons per minute
for a period of at least thirty minutes. Where more than one standpipe is
required, the minimum supply shall be 500 gallons per minute for the first
standpipe and 250 gallons per each additional standpipe, for a period of at
least thirty minutes. The supply shall be sufficient to maintain a residual
pressure of sixty-five pounds per square inch at the topmost outlet of each
standpipe, including the roof outlet, with 500 gallons per minute flowing from
the primary standpipe and 100 gallons per minute flowing from each additional
standpipe up to maximum flow of 900 gallons per minute. Such test shall be
performed in the presence of the Fire Chief and a written record of the results
shall be filed with the Fire Chief’s office prior to occupancy of the building.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1436.10 SPRINKLER SYSTEM CONNECTION THREADS AND CAPS.
   (a)   Every sprinkler system shall be equipped with one or more approved
Fire Division connections.
   (b)   There shall be a Fire Division hose connection on each street frontage
or, when the building sets back of the street lines, on each accessible
exterior wall. However, when a frontage or exterior wall is less than fifty
feet in length, no connection will be required on that frontage if the required
connections are provided on the other frontages.
   (c)   The thread of such connection shall be uniform with that used by the
Fire Division. Substantial caps shall be provided on each connection.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1436.11 PROTECTION FOR PLACES OF OUTDOOR ASSEMBLY.
   Fire-extinguishing equipment shall be furnished by the person operating,
conducting or promoting an affair in an outdoor place of assembly, unless such
equipment is otherwise furnished. The equipment shall be in kind and amounts
deemed adequate for the purpose by the Fire Chief and shall be located as
directed by the Chief. The equipment shall be in good working order.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1436.12 AMUSEMENT PARK PROTECTION.
   Within the grounds of every amusement park, properly placed fire hydrants
shall be installed and connected by a system of pipes to an adequate water
supply, with sufficient properly housed hose to reach into each building. All
equipment shall be designed to fit Fire Division equipment.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1436.13 BOWLING ALLEY PROTECTION.
   Fire-extinguishing equipment shall be provided and located in bowling alleys
as required by the Fire Chief.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1436.14 AUTOMATIC FIRE DETECTION SERVICE FOR CERTAIN BUILDINGS.
   (a)   All buildings housing ten or more persons and which are hereafter
erected or converted to be used as nursing homes, rest homes for the aged,
mental nursing homes, convalescent homes, alcoholic nursing homes, child day
care agencies and nurseries, boarding homes for handicapped or feebleminded
children, and boarding homes for children, shall be equipped with an automatic
fire detection service. This service shall provide operational coverage of the
entire building and shall be installed and maintained in accordance with
approved standards that conform to N.F.P.A. Standard Number 72. Such automatic
fire detection service shall be directly connected to the City’s fire alarm
system.
   (b)   Within one year from the effective date of this chapter, every
building specified in subsection (a) hereof shall provide an automatic fire
detection system which shall conform to N.F.P.A. Standard Number 72.
   (c)   All installations and inspections shall be under the jurisdiction of
the Division of Building and Zoning Inspection and the Fire Division. All
electrical installations shall comply with the National Electrical Code as
adopted by the City and amended from time to time.
   (d)   All buildings specified in subsection (a) hereof shall have auxiliary
emergency electrical systems which comply with Chapter 4101:2-27 of the Ohio
Basic Building Code.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1436.15 EMERGENCY POWER FOR FIRE PUMPS.
   All fire pumps shall be automatically switched to an emergency power circuit
of sufficient capacity to operate for a minimum of thirty minutes in the event
of power failure, or be powered by an independent power source.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1436.16 AUTOMATIC ALARMS AND DETECTORS REQUIRED IN CERTAIN BUILDINGS AND
STRUCTURES.
   All new buildings or structures the construction of which commences after
the date on which this Building and Housing Code becomes effective, which are
seventy-five feet or less in height and in which sleeping accommodations are
provided for the owners, users or occupants hereof, shall be provided with
approved automatic alarms and detectors of the products of combustion,
installed and maintained in accordance with the 1974 National Fire Protection
Association Pamphlet No. 74, to provide level four protection. However, nothing
in this section shall be construed to excuse the compliance with more stringent
requirements which are imposed upon buildings or structures by other provisions
of this Building and Housing Code or by provisions of any State Fire or
Building Code.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1436.99 PENALTY.
   (EDITOR’S NOTE: See Section
1422.99 for general Building and Housing Code penalty if no specific penalty is
provided.)
CHAPTER 1437
Rapid Access Key Box
1437.01   Definitions.
1437.02   Properties requiring rapid access key boxes.
1437.03   Placement of rapid access key boxes.
1437.04   Contents of key boxes.
1437.05   Compliance.
1437.99   Penalty.
1437.01 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purposes of this chapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   (a)   "Automatic Alarm." A system that does not require human intervention,
which is supervised by a central monitoring station.
   (b)   "Automatic Gate." A gate that is electronically controlled.
   (c)   "Central Monitoring Station." An office to which remote alarm and
supervisory signaling devices are transmitted, and where personnel are
constantly monitoring for alarms which indicate emergency conditions.
   (d)   "Hazardous Material." Any substance or material, be it chemical,
biological, radiological, or explosive in nature, which could cause harm to
humans, domestic animals, wildlife, agricultural crops, or property, when
released into the environment.
   (e)   "Key Switch." An approved UL type switch that can be operated by the
Fire Department to gain access through a locked gate.
   (f)   "Material Safety Data Sheets." Hereinafter referred to as "MSDS."
   (g)   "Rapid Access Key Box." A UL type, high security key vault for
emergency access to a specified structure.
   (h)   "Security Padlock." A padlock used by the Fire Department, which
enables access through a secured gate.
   (i)   "Superfund Amendments and Reauthorization Act of 1986." Hereinafter
referred to as "SARA."
(Ord. 69-2005. Passed 10-11-05.)
1437.02 PROPERTIES REQUIRING RAPID ACCESS KEY BOXES.
   Those industrial or commercial properties that meet at least one of the
following:
   (a)   All new and existing premises with any of the following:
      (1)   Monitored automatic alarm systems;
      (2)   Elevator;
      (3)   Automatic fire suppression systems.
   (b)   All new and existing residential complexes of four or more living
units, which are served by a main entrance that is secured.
   (c)   All new and existing premises with an "H" use group.
   (d)   All premises with automatic gates that impede access through
driveways, roads, or streets.
   (e)   All premises protected by secured fences or gates.
(Ord. 69-2005. Passed 10-11-05.)
1437.03 PLACEMENT OF RAPID ACCESS KEY BOXES.
   The placement of the key boxes shall be approved by the Fire Department.
(Ord. 69-2005. Passed 10-11-05.)
1437.04 CONTENTS OF KEY BOXES.
   (a)   As deemed necessary by the Fire Chief or his or her designee, key
boxes may be required to have any of the following.
      (1)   Keys to locked points of access;
      (2)   Keys to locked mechanical rooms;
      (3)   Keys to locked elevator rooms;
      (4)   Keys to elevator controls;
      (5)   Keys to any fenced or secured area;
      (6)   Keys to alarm panel;
      (7)   Any other keys as requested by Fire Chief or his or her designee;
      (8)   A card containing names and phone numbers of emergency contact
persons;
      (9)   Floor plans.
   (b)   Those premises with automatic gates or security padlocks must have a
rapid access key switch or a rapid access security padlock on the secured
fence.
   (c)   Premises that have hazardous materials stored on-site are additionally
required to have the following:
      (1)   A current emergency and hazardous chemical inventory as per Section
312 of SARA.
      (2)   A binder containing the MSDS required under Subtitle B, Section 311
of SARA, or, in the event of a volume of MSDS too large to keep in the lock
box, the information in the lock box must give the location of the on-site
sheets, which must be readily available for use by emergency personnel.
      (3)   A site plan, which shall include the following:
         A.   The location of storage and use of hazardous materials on-site.
         B.   The location of on-site emergency fire fighting and spill cleanup
equipment.
         C.   A diagram of the complete sewer system, water system, fire
hydrants and topographical information relative to the facility.
         D.   A copy of the Fire Department's preplan of the facility.
(Ord. 69-2005. Passed 10-11-05.)
1437.05 COMPLIANCE.
   All new premises must comply prior to assuming occupancy. All existing
structures which are required to have installed a rapid access key box as set
forth in Section
1437.02 must comply within six months from the effective date of this chapter.
(Ord. 69-2005. Passed 10-11-05.)
1437.99 PENALTY.
   Whoever violates this chapter is guilty of a minor misdemeanor. Each day
that such violation continues shall be considered a separate violation.
(Ord. 69-2005. Passed 10-11-05.)

1438.01 SAFEGUARDS TO REDUCE FIRE OR EXPLOSION HAZARDS.
   When, in the opinion of the Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection
or the Fire Chief, an existing or proposed occupancy, operation, act, process,
device or circumstance causes or will cause an undue fire or explosion hazard
to a building, to the occupants thereof or to the public, the Superintendent or
the Fire Chief shall have authority to require such reasonable alterations,
additions, safeguards or actions as may be necessary to eliminate or adequately
reduce such hazard.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1438.02 CONSTRUCTION OF FIRE-RETARDANT CEILINGS.
   Fire-retardant ceilings shall be constructed in accordance with one of the
following specifications:
   (a)   No less than three-quarter inch plaster on expanded metal lath
securely attached to steel supports by wire or special metal fasteners, not
over six inches on center, or, in buildings whose types of construction permit
wood framing, attached to wood supports by not smaller than one and one-half
inches eleven gauge, seven-sixteenths inch head-barbed roofing nails not over
six inches on center, or by equivalent staples. Plaster shall consist of one
part gypsum to not over two parts sand for the scratch coat and one part gypsum
to not over three parts sand for the brown coat, or shall consist of Portland
cement and sand in the same proportions, except that three pounds of asbestos
fiber shall be added with each bag of cement.
   (b)   In buildings whose types of construction permit wood framing, not less
than one-half inch plaster, consisting of one part gypsum to not over two parts
sand, on three-eighths inch perforated gypsum lath with one perforation of not
less than three-fourths inch diameter for not more than sixteen square inches
of lath surface, attached to wood supports by nails not smaller than one and
one-eighth inches long with three-eighths inch diameter heads, spaced not more
than four inches on center. Three-inch wide strips of expanded metal lath shall
be nailed over all joints in the gypsum lath with nails not smaller than one
and three-fourths inches long with one-half inch heads.
   (c)   Any combination floor and ceiling construction having a fire-
resistance rating of one hour or more.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1438.03 WOOD SHINGLES.
   (a)   Roofs on buildings used as one, two or three-family dwellings, or as
private garages, which are less than three stories or thirty-five feet in
height and which do not exceed 2,500 square feet in area, may be covered with
wood shingles. Wood shingles shall not be used on any building except where not
less than fifteen-feet clear distance will be maintained between such building
and any adjacent building. Such roofs shall be of approved vertical grain or
edge grain wooden shingles of a thickness not less than five butts in two
inches. The exposure of such wood shingles to the weather shall not exceed the
following:
      (1)   On roofs greater than one-third pitch, the exposure shall be five
inches for sixteen-inch shingles, five and one-half inches for eighteen-inch
shingles, and seven and one-half inches for twenty-four inch shingles;
      (2)   On roofs with less than one-third pitch, but not less than one-
quarter pitch, the exposure shall be greater than four inches for sixteen-inch
shingles, four and one-half inches for eighteen-inch shingles, and six and one-
half inches for twenty-four inch shingles.
   (b)   All wood shingles shall be securely nailed to the roof deck with rust-
resistant nails according to accepted good practice.
   (c)   In no case shall wood shingles be used unless they are approved by the
Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection in accordance with the
provisions of this section.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1438.04 COOLING TOWERS.
   (a)   Cooling towers, wherever located, shall not exceed forty percent of
the supporting roof area and shall be so constructed that the fire hazard
created thereby is reduced as much as is practicable.
   (b)   When a public nuisance is or will be caused by reason of mist or spray
from a cooling tower, the tower shall be adequately screened or enclosed with
noncombustible materials to prevent such nuisance.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1438.05 CORNICES.
   Cornices, including those on show windows, placed on buildings over fifty
feet in height shall be on noncombustible materials.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1438.06 INSPECTION OF FIRESTOPPING.
   No firestopping shall be covered or concealed until inspected by the
Superintendent of Building and Zoning Inspection or his or her authorized
representative.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1438.07 FIRESTOPPING OF JOISTS.
   Joists in all types of construction shall be firestopped at the ends and
over supports for the full depth of the joists.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1438.08 PREVENTION OF FIRE SPREAD IN ATTIC SPACES.
   In buildings of Type 4 (wood frame) construction, attic spaces shall be
divided into areas of 3,000 square feet or less by tight draft stops. These
shall be of two thicknesses of one-inch lumber with joints broken or the
equivalent, with access doors of similar construction. The Superintendent of
Building and Zoning Inspection may permit other adequate methods or appliances
for the prevention of the spread of fire in attic spaces.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1438.09 CONSTRUCTION OF FIRE PARTITIONS.
   (a)   Fire partitions shall have fire-resistance ratings of not less than
two hours. They shall be constructed of approved masonry or reinforced concrete
or other approved forms of construction of noncombustible materials. Fire
partitions may be used for load bearing, provided that, in addition to meeting
the requirements of this section, they conform to the requirements of this
Building and Housing Code for bearing walls.
   (b)   Fire partitions shall be supported in each story of construction
having a fire- resistance rating of not less than two hours. However, when they
also are load bearing, the supporting construction shall have a fire-resistance
rating of not less than four hours in case the building is of Type 1
(fireproof) construction or Type 2 (noncombustible) construction, and not less
than two hours in buildings of other types of construction.
   (c)   The maximum unsupported height of a fire partition of masonry
construction shall be thirty times its total thickness, unless suitably
anchored and reinforced, and the length between intermediate supports or
bracing shall not exceed twenty feet.
   (d)   Fire partitions shall be deemed continuous, even though the several
parts are not directly over one another in successive stories, if the
intervening parts of the floors at the levels where offsets occur are unpierced
and of Type 1 (fireproof) construction or Type 2 (noncombustible) construction
and all parts not supported directly on the foundations are carried on Type 1
(fireproof) construction.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1438.10 FIRE PARTITIONS IN BUILDINGS OF TYPE 3 CONSTRUCTION.
   In buildings of Type 3 (exterior masonry wall) construction, fire
partitions, if required in a story as a horizontal exit, shall be continuous
through all stories from the foundation to the roof.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1438.11 OPENINGS IN FIRE PARTITIONS.
   (a)   Required fire partitions shall have no openings other than required
door openings or properly protected duct openings.
   (b)   Openings in required fire partitions shall be equipped with approved
fire doors set in approved door frames.
   (c)   Each opening in a fire partition serving as a horizontal exit shall be
protected by an approved self-closing fire door.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1438.12 CELLAR CEILINGS.
   Except in one, two and three-family dwellings, the cellar or basement
ceilings of all buildings hereafter erected, or altered to change their
occupancy classification, which are not otherwise protected by fire-resistant
floor construction or by approved automatic sprinklers over the cellar, shall
conform to the requirements for fire-retardant ceilings provided in Section
1438.02.
(Ord. 42-1981. Passed 2-23-81.)
1438.99 PENALTY.
   (EDITOR’S NOTE: See Section
1422.99 for general Building and Housing Code penalty if no specific penalty is
provided.)
